title: DOM events, cleanup, and resource ownership
outcome: Trace event propagation and release listeners, timers, observers, and subscriptions with their owner.
useCase: Route transitions, realtime UI, resize handling, and forms.
benefits: Fewer duplicate actions and retained screens.
drawbacks: Resource ownership is separate from rendering correctness.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: If you open it, own its close.

trace.title: Mount owner
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

An event travels through capture, target, and bubble phases when the event supports propagation. target is where it originated; currentTarget is the element whose handler is running.

Event delegation puts a handler on a stable ancestor and checks the relevant descendant. It is useful for dynamic lists, but needs a precise match and containment check.

preventDefault cancels a supported default action. stopPropagation changes event propagation. They solve different problems.

A button inside a form defaults to submit unless its type says otherwise. Correct HTML often avoids a JavaScript workaround.

Every long-lived resource needs an owner: window listener, timer, ResizeObserver, WebSocket, and subscription. Vue watchers created synchronously in setup are linked to the component; manually created resources still need cleanup.

A watcher created later outside that scope may need explicit disposal.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Open a screen → register resource → use it → navigate away → cleanup → reopen. Observe that only one listener/subscription remains active.

Repeated mounting should not multiply calls.

For a nested icon click, compare target with currentTarget before reading dataset values. A handler attached to the button can use currentTarget for the button's data.

Do not trust DOM attributes as server authorization.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Repeated route visits can accumulate listeners and duplicate saves. A Cancel button without type=button can accidentally submit a form. stopPropagation does not automatically prevent navigation or form submission.
